title: Acceptance for a correct matrix product
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be square matrices of the same finite size over the field with two elements. If $C=AB$, then a uniformly random vector $x$ over that field satisfies $Cx=A(Bx)$ in every coordinate with probability $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $n$ is a natural number specifying the matrix size
